tools.name: get_health
tools.title: Service health: worker heartbeat and data freshness
tools.description:
Rolls up whether the ingest worker is running, which feed families (ndbc, coops, nws, openmeteo, goes19, coastwatch...) have stale sources, government dataset status and the GLM lightning feed. status is ok | degraded | down; HTTP 503 only when down. Check this before trusting 'no data' from other tools. detail=true lists every source.

Units: ft, kt, s, F, mi; directions FROM. Returns data and source/freshness metadata.

tools.name: list_spots
tools.title: List the defined spots (inlets, beaches, sandbars, reefs, offshore)
tools.description:
Every named South Florida spot the app scores, with its lat/lon, kind, region and the NOAA stations used for it. Use the returned id with conditions, forecast, tides, hazards and briefing tools. include=status adds the current-hour go/caution/nogo band per activity.
Use this for a map of verified coastal spots: the MCP app panel renders an interactive Florida map with selectable spots, nearby camera markers and conditions. Coordinates are geographic locations, not safe navigation routes.
Units: ft, kt, s, F, mi; directions FROM. Returns data and source/freshness metadata.

tools.name: get_spot

tools.description:
A single spot record plus now.scores (go/caution/nogo per activity for the current hour) when the worker has scored it.

Units: ft, kt, s, F, mi; directions FROM. Returns data and source/freshness metadata.

tools.name: get_conditions
tools.title: Conditions for a spot: now, 7-day hourly, tides, scores, alerts, hazards
tools.description:
The full conditions bundle for a named spot: current waves (ft, s, deg FROM), wind (kt), tide (ft MLLW), water temp (F), activity scores with reasons, 7-day hourly forecast, hi/lo tides, best windows, NWS alerts, rip/red tide/bacteria hazards, lightning and an AI briefing. Kitesurf: kiteboarding contains rider-specific weather screening and unverified launch status; supply kiteStyle, kiteExperience, kiteMinWindKt and kiteMaxWindKt. No overall kite score or verified launch is implied. Activities: kite, surf, skim (flatland), skim-wave (wave riding), paddle (flatwater paddleboard), sup-surf (SUP surf). Skim scores are absent without shoreline observations; do not substitute other activity scores. Prefer view=summary unless you need every hour. boat=<id> adds boat-specific chop comfort. For an arbitrary lat/lon use get_point_conditions.
Start here for a current spot question with view=summary: this single result includes forecast, tides, scores, advisories, hazards, lightning and source status. Avoid duplicate hazard/tide calls unless a needed detail is absent. For beach questions, sea-model wave heights and NWS breaking-surf heights measure different things; their difference alone is not a forecast conflict. A swim no-go must not be followed by a recommendation to wade.
Interpretation: omit boat unless the user supplied or confirmed it. Describe lightning as flashes observed or not detected in the stated window, never a clear/safe guarantee. Report unavailable/QC-failed sources even when freshness.stale=false; fresh does not mean every source is usable. Model sea height is not breaking surf height. Tide heights at different local MLLW gauges do not establish relative channel depths. High tide is not necessarily slack current. For kitesurfing use get_conditions with kiteStyle (freeride/waves/foil), kiteExperience and rider-supplied kiteMinWindKt/kiteMaxWindKt. Read kiteboarding for weather screening, gust spread and explicitly unverified launch status. Never infer the rider wind range, legal launch access or rescue coverage. Activity keys: kite, surf, skim (flatland), skim-wave (wave riding), paddle (flatwater paddleboard), sup-surf (SUP surf). Skim suitability is unscored without shoreline observations; missing scores must not inherit another activity. Offshore wind can favor surf while increasing paddleboard drift risk. A point depth cannot prove route clearance. Do not invent detection percentages, future readings, vessel ownership, or app settings instructions.
Units: ft, kt, s, F, mi; directions FROM. Returns data and source/freshness metadata.

tools.name: get_lightning
tools.title: Lightning status near a point, or for every spot
tools.description:
GOES-19 GLM lightning. With lat+lon: level (clear | watch 10-25 mi | danger < 10 mi in the last 5 min), nearest strike distance (mi) and time, strikes in 15 min, all-clear time (30 min after the last strike within 10 mi), SPC thunder outlook, and the last 30 min of flashes. Without lat/lon: status per spot. When the feed is stale, status is null and unavailableReason explains why (never a false 'clear').
Prefer list_spots for named spot coordinates. State no flashes detected in the observed window rather than no lightning exists. Stale/incomplete coverage means unknown. Do not supply detection rates that are absent from this result.

tools.name: get_dataset
tools.title: One government dataset
tools.description:
The latest payload of one dataset from list_datasets, including sharks and jellyfish. These marine-life records are dated observations, not live beach warnings; no records does not imply absence. bbox filters list datasets; category filters USCG notices (e.g. bridge,hazard); homeZone=true limits discharges to the home zone; geometry=true includes MPA polygons. 503 when the dataset has never loaded.
Shark, jellyfish and man-of-war records are dated published observations, not live tracking, beach warnings, abundance estimates or swimming-safety scores. Preserve observation dates, uncertainty, attribution and source availability. No records does not mean the animals are absent. Source checked time is not observation time. Man-of-war are siphonophores, not true jellyfish. Local lifeguard links are not ingested current warnings; check the source report date. Never apply NOAA's Chesapeake sea-nettle forecast to Florida.
Units: ft, kt, s, F, mi; directions FROM. Returns data and source/freshness metadata.

tools.name: plan_route

tools.description:
Chart-aware water routing between from/to spot IDs or lat,lon. Supply a confirmed library boat ID or measured draft, with beam, airDraft, ukc, bridgeMargin and speed overrides in feet/knots. Checks chart depths and tides along the geometry, samples across supplied beam, identifies bridges and restrictions, checks predicted MHW bridge clearance when data permits, and adds route weather samples. Does not infer saved vessel settings. Supports ordered via stops and a hard corridor=icw constraint. Cold charts may take 110 seconds.
Interpretation: omit boat unless the user supplied or confirmed it. Describe lightning as flashes observed or not detected in the stated window, never a clear/safe guarantee. For kitesurfing use get_conditions with kiteStyle (freeride/waves/foil), kiteExperience and rider-supplied kiteMinWindKt/kiteMaxWindKt. Skim suitability is unscored without shoreline observations; missing scores must not inherit another activity. Offshore wind can favor surf while increasing paddleboard drift risk. A point depth cannot prove route clearance. Do not invent detection percentages, future readings, vessel ownership, or app settings instructions.

tools.name: get_chop_history
tools.title: Canonical chop history and trends
tools.description:
Gillby's native 0-10 chop series for up to 31 days, daily mean/max, coverage and 7-day trends. Recorded outputs and historical model reconstructions are identified separately. Never replace these with assistant-defined Calm/Moderate/Rough cutoffs or fabricate gaps.
For chop history or trends use get_chop_history with a verified spot ID. Preserve recorded versus reconstructed provenance, native 0–10 index and labels, coverage and gaps. Never invent assistant-defined rough/calm thresholds or silently substitute wave/wind series for native chop.
Units: ft, kt, s, F, mi; directions FROM. Returns data and source/freshness metadata.

tools.name: get_history
tools.title: Stored environmental history
tools.description:
Read stored observations or forecast history for source and var. Forecast source uses forecast:model and requires spot. Maximum window 31 days; up to 1000 points. Latest revision/run wins. Rejected and suspect rows are excluded; unreviewed rows retain quality metadata.
For chop history or trends use get_chop_history with a verified spot ID. Preserve recorded versus reconstructed provenance, native 0–10 index and labels, coverage and gaps. Never invent assistant-defined rough/calm thresholds or silently substitute wave/wind series for native chop.
Units: ft, kt, s, F, mi; directions FROM. Returns data and source/freshness metadata.
